subject: Control-plane storyboard and egress mapping for Dedicated/Private — request
messages:
From: Frank Liu <frank.liu@acme-payments.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com; Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private/Dedicated network isolation — control-plane storyboard and egress map request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our internal SIG-lite review and the procurement packet we need a concise narrative + visuals that tie the control-plane separation to egress controls for a Dedicated/Private deployment. Specifically: a storyboard (step-by-step flow) showing how a request from an ACME tenant is routed, where KV-cache and prefix caching live, and an egress translation table that lists which external destinations (SaaS logs, telemetry endpoints) are allowed per tenancy.

Deliverables ideally:
- One consolidated PDF storyboard (single page per step) with callouts
- CSV with egress translation rules and justification
- Annotated PNG of the isolation diagram highlighting control vs data plane boundaries

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the above and a short statement about fallback behavior (automatic model variant fallback when capacity constrained) for our auditors? We have a SIG submission deadline 2026-08-20.

Thanks,
Frank
Security Architecture Lead
Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Private/Dedicated network isolation — control-plane storyboard and egress map request

Hi Frank —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can produce the three deliverables you listed and include a short, auditor-friendly statement on fallback behavior. Plan:

1) Storyboard PDF (ctrlplane-storyboard-v1.pdf) — stepwise flow from tenant request to inference response; we’ll call out the control-plane components (placement/orchestration, key-rotation, routing policy) vs data-plane (inference runtime, KV cache, model replicas).
2) Egress translation CSV (egress-translation-table.csv) — mapping of internal service roles to external FQDNs/IP ranges, rationale, and minimal retention notes.
3) Annotated isolation diagram (isolation-diagram-annotated.png) — high level topology with control-plane arrows and shaded trust boundaries.

We expect to have draft artifacts by COB 2026-08-12 for your review. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we scope correctly:
- Do you want per-region (us/eu) egress lists or a consolidated global table?
- For fallback behavior, do you need our standard public-hosted fallback text or one that references your Dedicated routing policy (we can redact tenant ids)?

I’ll loop Kim to collect the diagram exports and Vivek for the fallback statement and egress rationale.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Lead, Product Security (Redwood Inference)
T: +1 415 555 0143

Subject: Re: Private/Dedicated network isolation — control-plane storyboard and egress map request

Frank / Soojin —

Attached: ctrlplane-storyboard-v1.pdf, isolation-diagram-annotated.png, egress-translation-table.csv (samples). Notes:

- Storyboard: 5 steps covering (1) tenant API call enters ingress LB, (2) routing decision and model variant selection in control plane, (3) placement to Dedicated pool and KV cache hit/miss behavior, (4) inference execution in data-plane, (5) response and selective telemetry export. Each step has a short justification and mapped trust boundary.
- Egress table: rows include service (metrics/logs/agent-updates), destination (FQDN + CIDR), allowed-tenancy (shared/admin-only/dedicated), retention, and justification. We marked telemetry endpoints that use TLS + mTLS.
- Fallback statement (excerpt): "When Dedicated capacity is not available within configured latency SLOs, Redwood will route to pre-approved model variants within the same region based on customer policy. Data-plane artifacts (KV cache) are not migrated to fallback endpoints; fallbacks are policy-limited and only used for read-only inference requests where the customer has enabled cross-pool fallback."

A couple of items for ACME to confirm so we finalize:
1) Confirm whether you need the per-tenant CIDR suppression (we can redact to role-level groups if you prefer).
2) Do you require signed attestations or just the artifact bundle for SIG/SOC2 review?

If all good, we’ll prepare a signature-ready PDF and a CSV with IP ranges expanded by region.

Kimberly Park
Director, Cloud Security (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: ctrlplane-storyboard-v1.pdf (23 KB), isolation-diagram-annotated.png (744 KB), egress-translation-table.csv (2 KB)

We will attach the three files to the SIG Lite packet and include the attestation as a supporting doc.
